Theorem
[Sectional Curvatures of the Model Spaces] ↗ ex:shape-operators-spheres 1. ch8:8.34

The model spaces have constant sectional curvatures

  1. $0$ on $(\mathbb R^n,\bar g)$;

  2. $1/R^2$ on $(\mathbb S^n(R),\bar g_R)$;

  3. $-1/R^2$ on $(\mathbb H^n(R),\bar g_R)$.

Proof

\sketch Euclidean space has zero curvature tensor, hence zero sectional curvature. For the round sphere, the shape operator is $-(1/R)\operatorname {Id}$, so the Gauss equation gives sectional curvature $(-1/R)^2=1/R^2$; frame homogeneity makes this value constant.

□

For each $c\in \mathbb R$, exactly one of these model families has constant sectional curvature $c$, with its radius determined by $|c|^{-1/2}$ when $c\ne 0$.
